title: incident-bot: improve oncall diagnostics & runbook link resolution
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Enhances incident-bot on-call diagnostic output with deterministic runbook link resolution, improved SLO correlation hints, and static checks to avoid broken links in runbooks.
description:
Motivation: On-call responders frequently reach for runbook links in incident-bot summaries, but we found two issues: (1) runbook links were generated from heuristics that produced false-positives for similarly named playbooks, and (2) missing metadata made SLO->runbook correlation brittle during high-noise incidents. This PR improves diagnostics and runbook linkage to reduce cognitive load during incidents and surface actionable context for fast resolution.

What it does (summary): added a deterministic runbook_linker that resolves canonical runbook URLs using a small prioritized matcher (linear + tag hints + title exact match), exposes runbook suggestions in the oncall summary payload, and augments SLO correlation with confidence scores and quick-reason snippets. Also introduced a CI static-check script to validate runbook link integrity at PR time and added unit + integration tests for edge cases.

Checklist: 
- [x] deterministic runbook matcher implementation
- [x] include runbook suggestions in oncall diagnostic payload
- [x] add confidence score & snippet for SLO correlation
- [x] unit + integration tests
- [x] CI static link checker
- [x] update docs (oncall runbook docs)

Commits (high-level): one squashable feature branch: 
- add runbook_linker+matcher with prioritization rules
- wire runbook suggestions into diagnostics payload
- expose confidence score and snippet in SLO correlation service
- add runbook link static-check script and CI integration
- tests + docs + minor telemetry metrics

Files changed (high-level): pkg/diagnostics/runbook_linker.go - new deterministic matcher and canonicalizer; pkg/diagnostics/runbook_linker_test.go - unit tests for fuzzy/title/tag matching; pkg/oncall/summary_builder.go - include runbook suggestions (url, confidence, reason) in summary payload; internal/slo/slo_matcher.go - add confidence and reason fields to correlation output; scripts/ci/runbook-static-checks.sh - new CI step that validates links referenced in runbook registry; docs/oncall/runbooks.md - docs for how runbook resolution works; deploy/k8s/incident-bot-deployment.yaml - bump config to enable new diagnostics flag.

Review conversation (summary):
- Ethan: "Nice approach, can we avoid hitting registry on hot paths?" 
- Ava: "We cache canonical mappings in-memory with a TTL and fall back to a lightweight title-prefix index to keep latency <2ms on hot paths."\n- Priya: "Confidence score computation looks okay but please call out threshold defaults in docs." 
- Ava: "Added defaults to docs and exposed config via ENV with reasonable defaults."\n- Lucas: "CI script should also fail on redirects to external hosts; add a check."\n- Ava: "Added redirect validation and a whitelist check for known hosts."

CI summary: initial run had an integration test flake in slo_matcher (timing-dependent) which I fixed by adding a small backoff/retry in the test harness. Final CI: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass (rerun), lint: pass, static-runbook-check: pass.

Merge: approved by reviewers after one round of changes, merged to main via squash on 2025-11-20 (merge commit 9f3b2c7).

Why this matters: during recent oncall rotations we observed responders spending >30s locating the canonical runbook for common alerts; this change reduces that friction and should measurably cut mean time to acknowledge/resolve for correlated SLO alerts.

Notes: this is backward-compatible (feature gated via ENABLE_RUNBOOK_SUGGESTIONS), no customer-facing API changes. Follow-ups: track adoption metrics/CTR for suggested runbooks and iterate matching rules based on false-positive signal (ENG-5893).
